title: The Strength of Root Cuts in an Extended Abstract Branch-and-Cut Model
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31774v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The branch-and-cut paradigm has led to effective solvers for a wide range of mathematical optimization problems. Despite significant theoretical work on pure branching and pure cutting, less is known about their interaction. We study an extended abstract branch-and-cut model to investigate tradeoffs between branching and cutting, including the time to generate cuts. We prove that, under symmetric branching, some minimal-time tree has all cuts at the root, before the first branching node, and that there is an asymmetric setting where some minimal-time tree has no internal cuts, i.e., cuts both preceded and followed by branching. For other settings, although a root-cut tree may be suboptimal and differ substantially in structure from a minimal-time tree, it nevertheless provides a reliable approximation whose tree time does not deviate arbitrarily from the optimum. For constant cut strength and bounded time functions, we show that the best root-cut tree is asymptotically optimal as the target bound grows. In addition, under a single-cut-per-path restriction, we characterize when some minimal-time tree has an internal cut. Lastly, simulations indicate that the best root-cut tree is much closer to a minimal-time tree than our worst-case approximation guarantee suggests.

title: Ozone groups and centers of two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras
authors: James G\'omez, H\'ector Su\'arez, Helbert Venegas
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31781v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $p,q$ be roots of unity with $pq\neq1$, and put $\ell=|\langle p,q\rangle|$ and $t=\ord(pq)$. Up to isomorphism, the two-parameter quantum Heisenberg algebras $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ are exactly the noetherian PI graded down-up algebras, so everything here holds for that whole class. The ozone group is $\mu_\ell\times\mu_{\ell/t}$, generated by conjugation by three normal elements, and the center is recovered from the fixed ring of the ozone group as the invariants of a cyclic group of order $t$. We give a presentation of the center as a hypersurface over a cyclic quotient surface singularity. It is regular exactly when $1$ is a characteristic root, which disproves a conjecture of Chan, Gaddis, Won and Zhang, and Gorenstein exactly when $p^{m/h}=q^{n/h}$, where $m=\ord(p)$, $n=\ord(q)$ and $h=\gcd(m,n)$; for $p=\zeta_5$, $q=\zeta_5^{2}$ it is not. We also decide when the fixed ring of the ozone group is Gorenstein and when $\mathcal H_{p,q}$ is Calabi--Yau, and show that the algebras with regular center have non-affine automorphisms and nonzero locally nilpotent derivations.

title: Rapid stabilization for Stokes and Navier-Stokes systems with localized disturbance
authors: Christian Calle, Patricio Guzm\'an, Hugo Parada, Jefferson Prada
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31790v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this study, we analyze the rapid stabilization of Stokes and the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems in the presence of an unknown spatially localized disturbance. A multivalued feedback control strategy is proposed which combines the Lyapunov frequency method with the multivalued sign operator. This methodology connects Lyapunov-based stability analysis with spectral inequalities, while the inclusion of the sign operator provides robustness against disturbance. The closed-loop system is governed by a differential inclusion, for which well-posedness is proved via the theory of maximal monotone operators. This approach guarantees global rapid exponential stabilization for the Stokes system and local rapid exponential stabilization for the two- and three-dimensional Navier-Stokes systems, with arbitrarily large disturbance bounds. In three dimensions, we obtain global strong solutions and rapid exponential stabilization for initial data sufficiently small in the $L^2$-norm with a prescribed, arbitrarily large bound in the $H^1$-norm.

title: Stochastic Geometry Meets Optimization: Data-Driven Cellular Planning
authors: Abhishek K. Shukla, Abhishek K. Gupta, Ketan Rajawat
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31793v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deployment optimization of base stations (BSs) is critical for improving cellular network performance metrics such as coverage and capacity, impacting user experience, scalability, and infrastructure cost-effectiveness. Traditional methods that optimize precise BS locations do not generally provide broader insights into spatial deployment priorities or alternative viable deployments. Stochastic geometry approaches, on the other hand, offer a more interpretable intensity-based framework, but rarely utilize real-world user location data or investigate optimal BS deployment strategies. In this work, we propose a data-driven stochastic geometry-based approach that optimizes BS deployment intensity to maximize a network performance metric using samples from an unknown user-location distribution. We specialize the framework to an inhomogeneous Poisson point process (PPP) for cellular coverage analysis. The resulting infinite-dimensional problem is discretized over the deployment area and solved using sampled user locations. We characterize the discretization and sampling errors, apply stochastic mirror ascent to solve the empirical problem, and analyze the selection of concrete BS deployments using independent validation samples. Unlike traditional methods, our approach yields an optimized spatial intensity that reveals deployment priorities across regions and accommodates practical deployment constraints, multi-tier networks, and incremental deployment scenarios. Numerical experiments with synthetic and real-world spatial demand data demonstrate the proposed approach under different network configurations.

title: Research profiles and the mathematical landscape: A grassroots proposal for mathematics with AI
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31804v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Repeated mathematical work with AI leaves behind corrections, failed arguments, and sometimes useful ways of asking questions. I propose keeping these in a research profile that the mathematician develops and controls. The profile marks parts of the mathematical landscape according to the researcher's understanding and makes those markings available to later work with AI. This suggests experiments with individual profiles, shared readings of papers, and graduate education. It also raises mathematical questions about the landscape itself: its connections, distances, and changes under discovery. I describe two examples, searching for branches of mathematics with a common base and recovering useful questions from the history of Floer theory. The aim is to give mathematicians something to try and a part in deciding how mathematical AI develops.

title: Finite element approximation on piecewise smooth domains
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31822v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The approximation theory by finite elements is usually described on the simplified geometry of polygonal or polyhedral domains. While avoiding the question of boundary approximation makes the analysis simpler, real applications may involve piecewise smooth domains and in some cases the extension of classical results to general boundaries may be tricky. In this paper we discuss in a systematic way the approximation properties and the error analysis of standard non-isoparametric finite element spaces on piecewise curvilinear domains in two and three dimensions. We show in detail how the geometric error introduces a barrier for the $H^1$ and $L^2$ error of the solution of both Dirichlet and Neumann elliptic problems independently of the regularity of the problem and of the degree of the finite element spaces used.

title: Higher-order asymptotic formulae for periodic orbits of 3-dimensional volume-preserving Anosov flows and the Foulon conjecture
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31823v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $X^t$ be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class $C^7$ on a closed $3$-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit $\gamma$, and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods $T_n$ and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers $\log\lambda_n$. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on $\gamma$. Following the idea of De Simoi-Leguil-Vinhage-Yang, we compare these asymptotics when volume is the measure of maximal entropy. In this case, the equilibrium-state characterizations of volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize periods and exponents: $\log\lambda_n=hT_n$. Matching the coefficients of the two asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of both cocycles to vanish.
  Then the work of Foulon-Hasselblatt on the longitudinal Anosov cocycle, together with Foulon's work on the contact case, yields the Foulon Conjecture for flows of class $C^7$: if volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then, up to a finite cover, $X^t$ is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the $2$-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.

title: Positive Planar Measures for Spectral Pinching and the Corrected BMV Conjecture
authors: Trung Hoa Dinh, Cong Trinh Le, Trung Dung Vuong
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31851v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove the corrected Bessis--Moussa--Villani pinching conjecture for all symmetrized word averages. For Hermitian matrices $A,B$ and $D=E_A(B)$, we construct a positive compactly supported measure $\zeta_{A,B}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ such that \[ \Tr f(xA+yB)-\Tr f(xA+yD) =y^2\int_{\mathbb R^2}f''(xa+yb)\,d\zeta_{A,B}(a,b). \] Its total mass is $\frac12\|B-D\|_2^2$. This representation proves the corrected conjecture, including its equality cases, and gives a positive bivariate moment representation for the coefficient differences. We also derive complete monotonicity of normalized exponential pinching defects and a comparison with Lie--Trotter approximations. A one-dimensional second-order loss measure is obtained for trace-preserving conditional expectations on finite tracial von Neumann algebras. Finally, we relate $\zeta_{A,B}$ to Hein\"avaara's tracial joint spectral measure by an explicit positive radial transform.

title: The permutation and automorphism groups of univariate multiplicity codes
authors: Eduardo Camps Moreno, Hiram H. L\'opez, Umberto Mart\'inez-Pe\~{n}as, Rodrigo San-Jos\'e
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31858v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We give explicit characterizations of the permutations and linear isometries that leave (univariate) multiplicity codes invariant. We consider any evaluation subset of the finite field, any multiplicity and dimension, and the automorphisms are with respect to the Niederreiter-Rosenblom-Tsfasman (NRT) metric. For multiplicity one, we recover the permutation and automorphism groups of classical Reed--Solomon codes in the classical Hamming metric. In the main dimension range, automorphisms are uniquely determined by a projectivity that permutes the evaluation subset, up to multiplication by a nonzero scalar. For multiplicity one, permutations are given by affine maps that permute the evaluation subset. In contrast, for multiplicity at least two, permutations are only given by translations that permute the evaluation subset. Finally, we give an algebraic characterization of automorphisms of multiplicity codes for the folded Hamming metric.

title: Multilevel Monte Carlo for Polytopic DG Discretisations with Spatially Represented Random Coefficients
authors: Veronika Chronholm, Matt Evans, Emmanuil H. Georgoulis, Tristan Pryer
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31861v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a multilevel Monte Carlo framework for coercive elliptic problems with random diffusion and reaction coefficients on polytopic meshes, with particular emphasis on the approximation and inter-level coupling of random coefficients generated from spatially represented latent fields. The main analytical contribution is a Strang-type error decomposition in a DG norm that separates the forward discretisation error from the error introduced by approximating the random coefficients. On this basis, we study two coefficient-generation and multilevel-coupling strategies, a spectral sampler based on a stationary Gaussian latent field defined on a fixed Cartesian reference grid, and an SPDE-based Mat\'ern sampler in which levels are coupled through projected white-noise loads on agglomerated hierarchies. Both fit into the same coefficient-aware analytical framework and couple adjacent levels directly through a common latent random input. The theory is supported by numerical experiments on general Voronoi and agglomerated polytopic meshes, demonstrating the predicted forward and coefficient-representation errors, decay of multilevel corrections, strong inter-level coupling, and the resulting work-accuracy behaviour relative to single-level Monte Carlo.

title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31872v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.

title: Observability from measurable sets for strongly coupled parabolic systems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31876v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We characterize observability of strongly coupled parabolic systems from arbitrary space-time measurable sets of positive measure. For constant coercive diffusion matrices and arbitrary constant zeroth-order coupling and observation matrices, observability holds if and only if the generalized Kalman rank condition is satisfied at every Dirichlet eigenvalue. The diffusion matrix need not be diagonalizable, and the number of components is arbitrary. The observation is measured in $L^1$, yielding null controllability with bounded controls by duality. The proof combines a Remez-type inequality for exponential polynomials with a quantitative analysis of the mode-dependent Kalman condition. The resulting finite-dimensional observability estimate is uniform over the spatial modes up to a polynomial frequency loss. A spectral inequality and the Lebeau--Robbiano strategy then give observability of the full system.

title: Polarized Ensemble Kalman Inversion: A Derivative-Free Method for Multimodal Inverse Problems with Non-asymptotic Analysis
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31907v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Inverse problems often admit multiple solutions consistent with the same noisy, indirect observations, especially with sparse data and/or strongly nonlinear forward models. Ensemble Kalman inversion (EKI) provides a robust, derivative-free framework to solve inverse problems, but its global empirical covariances couple all ensemble members across distinct solution modes, limiting its effectiveness for multimodal problems. We introduce polarized ensemble Kalman inversion (PEKI), which constructs distance-weighted local covariances for each ensemble member. This localization weakens contributions from distant, data-consistent regions and enables different clusters of ensemble members to evolve toward distinct solution modes. For the practical algorithm with finite ensemble size and polarization radius, we also establish non-asymptotic bounds and perform numerical studies, showing that cross-cluster effects decay exponentially with cluster separation relative to the polarization radius. For linear forward maps, we further establish particle-wise residual contraction and derive an exact cluster-mean decomposition that separates cross-cluster leakage, within-cluster gain variation, and observation perturbations. These results further motivate a one-step procedure for choosing the polarization radius by reusing stored forward-model evaluations. We studied the performance of PEKI on several numerical experiments, including low-dimensional nonconvex benchmarks, a problem equipped with many-mode landscape, and a high-dimensional inverse problem governed by Navier--Stokes equations. The results confirm the theoretical exponential decay of cross-cluster effects and show that PEKI can serve as a robust and derivative-free method for inverse problems with multiple solution modes.

title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31921v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach \`{a} la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on $\operatorname{BV}[0,1]$ associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.

title: Flexibility of topological entropy and factor persistence in the $C^0$-Gromov Hausdorff topology
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31939v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that every surjective topological dynamical system on a compact metric space can be approximated in the $C^0$-Gromov--Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with any prescribed topological entropy in $[0,+\infty]$, even when simultaneous approximation of its sets of invariant and ergodic measures is required. We also establish a rigidity result under uniform geometric bounds in a fixed dimension: for a homeomorphism of a closed, connected Riemannian manifold, topological stability in the sense of Gromov--Hausdorff guarantees its persistence as a factor of sufficiently close perturbations within the same geometric class. This persistence prevents topological entropy from decreasing and ensures that every invariant or ergodic measure of the original system admits a lift of the same type to the perturbed system.

title: Mean estimation in spatial functional data
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Functional mean estimation exhibits a sparse-to-dense phase transition as the number of measurements per curve increases. For spatially indexed functional data, however, dependence between nearby curves and increasing spatial sampling density fundamentally alter this transition. We investigate this phenomenon under a unified framework allowing both increasing-domain and infill asymptotics, with irregular temporal observations. Our analysis identifies two distinct sources of estimation error: an observation-level component governed by the total number of measurements and a curve-level component governed by a spatial dependence-adjusted effective sample size. The resulting uniform convergence rates reveal how spatial dependence shifts the temporal phase-transition boundary and how spatial infill can improve estimation through additional measurements without a corresponding increase in effective curve-level information. We establish these results for three spline-based estimators: a pooled estimator of a stationary mean curve, a local-kernel estimator, and a tensor-product estimator of a spatially varying mean surface. The effects of spatial localization on the phase transition are characterized explicitly. Simulations illustrate the interplay between spatial dependence and temporal sampling density, and environmental data applications demonstrate the proposed estimation methods.

title: Perturbed Exponential Systems, Pattern-Dependent Shifted-Sinc Operators, and Matrix Symbols on Finite Unions of Intervals
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study perturbed exponential systems and unions of shifted frequency lattices through shifted-sinc operators and finite-dimensional fiberizations. For the auxiliary binary local-shift model, we identify the exact pattern-dependent invariant $$ \rho_{\delta,s}=\|P_-T_{2\delta}P_+\|, $$ which gives the optimal squared synthesis bounds $1\pm\rho_{\delta,s}$. For periodic patterns, the synthesis operator reduces exactly to a single constant Vandermonde-type matrix, yielding finite-dimensional basis criteria and optimal bounds. We further prove that the worst binary lower bound is the infimum of its periodic counterparts; at the critical value $\delta=1/4$, a step pattern is governed by a half-shifted Hilbert matrix and has vanishing lower bound, although every fixed periodic pattern remains invertible.
  We also combine exact bounds for structured patterns with a support-independent perturbation estimate, obtaining explicit stability neighborhoods. For finite unions of bounded intervals and finitely many shifted lattices, folding modulo one yields finitely many rectangular phase matrices whose singular values and ranks give the exact bounds and complete Riesz-sequence, frame, and Riesz-basis criteria. This framework also yields finite Hadamard constraints for periodic spectra and an exact reduction of rationally commensurate multirate sampling.

title: Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics
authors: Eric Bedford, Rostislav Grigorchuk, Nguyen-Bac Dang, Mikhail Lyubich
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31961v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.

title: Closed-form Optimal Solutions for Propulsive-Differential Drag Control of Spacecraft Swarms
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper presents a novel optimal control approach for Distributed Space Systems (DSS) to minimize the total delta-v cost for large, time-constrained reconfigurations. Reconfiguration cost is decreased by blending differential drag and propulsive control within the same control window. By parameterizing the problem with Relative Orbital Elements (ROE) and leveraging reachable set theory, a maneuver planning methodology is derived to produce provably-optimal, full roto-translational control solutions in closed-form, such that they can be implemented on hardware-limited spacecraft.

title: Closed-form Optimal Propulsive-Differential Drag Control for Large Reconfigurations of Spacecraft Swarms
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31973v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distributed Space Systems offer unique capabilities but have significant hardware limitations on computational processing and fuel when employing small satellites. These constraints drive interest in deterministic maneuver planning that incorporates orbital perturbations to improve final state accuracy and decrease reconfiguration delta-v cost. This paper proposes a novel closed-form, provably optimal framework to generate complete roto-translational solutions for propulsive-differential drag control of multiple satellites. The approach leverages relative orbit elements and reachable set theory to characterize all control with a single methodology that can be readily generalized to generic impulsive-continuous control. The algorithm is robust to large reconfigurations and extended control windows where differential drag is most effective.

title: Optimal Graphon Control of Collective Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31975v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study optimal control of non-linear graphon dynamics in which the interaction kernel itself is the control. Motivated by opinion formation in social networks, we ask how changing who influences whom can steer a population toward a desired outcome. We develop a framework using interaction kernels with bounded variation in the receiver label, providing compactness while accommodating finite networks. We prove existence of an optimal pair and show that finite-agent approximations recover the continuum optimal value under successive refinement of the network and initial data, with subsequential convergence of suitably chosen discrete optimizers. Numerical experiments use neural networks to approximate optimal controls for bounded-confidence and graphon Kuramoto dynamics, illustrating how changes in interactions can prevent fragmentation and promote synchronization.

title: A Novel Matrix-Free Approximate Elemental Inverse for Efficient Preconditioning of Discontinuous Galerkin Spectral Elements
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31982v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient matrix-free preconditioning remains a challenge for discontinuous Galerkin spectral element discretisations of elliptic problems, particularly for general element shapes with collapsed-coordinate bases, such as prisms, tetrahedra and pyramids. Multigrid provides a promising framework, but its efficiency depends strongly on the effectiveness and computational cost of the smoother. For modal bases, point Jacobi can provide insufficient smoothing, whereas applying block Jacobi through stored dense inverses incurs substantial storage and computational costs. We propose a matrix-free approximate elemental inverse, an approximation to the inverse of each elemental diagonal block, constructed from inverse modal-to-nodal transforms and an element-dependent sparse matrix. Its application exploits generalised sum-factorisation and partial sum-factorisation in collapsed coordinates, avoiding the explicit storage and multiplication of large dense matrices. The method is evaluated as both a standalone preconditioner and a multigrid smoother on hexahedral, prismatic, tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. Although the proposed approximation generally increases iteration counts compared to exact block Jacobi, the cost per iteration is far lower. This trade-off yields substantial reductions in total solution time for hexahedral and prismatic elements, while achieving comparable performance for tetrahedral and pyramidal elements. This study can also serve as a practical guide for tuning the convergence of the discontinuous Galerkin interior-penalty Poisson solver.

title: A Globally Convergent Newton Method for Nonsmooth Optimization in the absence of Smooth Surrogates
authors: Tran T. A. Nghia, Nghia V. Vo, Khoa V. H. Vu
abstract:
arXiv:2610.31992v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose a globally convergent Newton method for convex composite optimization problems with polyhedral regularizers. The method rests on the observation that the proximal gradient step yields not only a new point but also a subgradient, which determines the face on which the linearization of the regularizer is exact. Minimizing a second-order model of the objective over this face produces a Newton direction that involves no generalized second-order information about the regularizer and is a descent direction for the objective itself. The method is therefore globalized by an Armijo line search on the original objective which, unlike forward-backward envelope techniques, requires only evaluations of the smooth component. We establish global convergence and local quadratic convergence to tilt-stable minimizers without any nondegeneracy condition, and show that the unit step is always accepted when the smooth component is quadratic, which yields a line-search-free method. The subproblems require only projections onto faces, which are explicit for the Lasso and nonnegative least squares and computable in linear time for the fused Lasso. Numerical experiments show that the method compares favorably with state-of-the-art solvers.

title: Strengthening AC optimal power flow relaxation through offline bound tightening and linear approximations
authors: Xiangxin An, Constance Crozier, Santanu S. Dey
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The alternating-current optimal power flow (ACOPF) problem is fundamental to power system operation and planning, but its nonconvexity makes globally optimal solutions of large-scale instances computationally challenging. Convex relaxations provide tractable lower bounds for assessing solution quality and supporting global optimization, although their effectiveness depends strongly on relaxation strength. This paper proposes an offline convexification and bound tightening framework for constructing strong linear programming (LP) relaxations for families of related ACOPF instances. Rather than repeating the tightening procedure for each instance, we compute variable bounds and second-order cone outer-approximation (SOC-OA) cuts offline using a demand-slack model and reuse them for subsequent instances with the same topology and admissible demand variations. Computational results on PGLib instances show that the fully offline approach achieves an average gap of $4.32\%$, compared with $3.80\%$ for the fully online approach, while achieving an average speedup of approximately $272\times$. The results demonstrate that offline convexification and bound tightening can recover most of the relaxation improvement of online tightening while significantly reducing the computational burden for repeated ACOPF evaluations.

title: Fisher Information and the Minimum Mean-Square Error for Locating Closely Spaced Point Sources
authors: Chuling Wen, Jian Lu, Qingtang Jiang, Charles K. Chui
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32018v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We determine the optimal average error of locating closely spaced sources from noisy superpositions of a known smooth response with unknown complex coefficients. Relative phases control how changes in one location can be offset by the other unknowns, so local Fisher information alone does not determine the attainable error. For every fixed number $K\ge2$ of sources with independent uniform phases, we prove matching Bayes risk bounds jointly in separation and noise, for all sufficiently small separations and all noise levels. Odd source counts have two risk regimes; even counts have an intermediate regime in which mean squared error is linear in the noise standard deviation. A projected least-squares estimator attains these orders without knowing the phases or the prior density. Bounded nonuniform phase laws preserve the orders under stated support conditions, whereas priors concentrated near poorly identified configurations can change the exponents. A common finite comparison yields both a global inverse bound and paths controlled by the original prior. These give sufficient conditions under which the risk has the order of the pointwise capped Cram\'er--Rao bound, and a lower-tail calculation explains the power and logarithmic regimes. We also give conditional guarantees when the cluster center, separation, and source count are unknown, with an additional low-noise requirement for count selection. A calibrated covariance factor model illustrates the same criterion beyond source localization.

title: On Exact Critical-Region Boundaries in Continuous-Time Multiparametric Optimal Control Problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32043v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Continuous-time multiparametric model predictive control solves the optimal control problem once, offline, for every initial state, and divides the initial-state space into critical regions, each with its own control law and sequence of active constraints. A boundary between two regions is either a hyperplane, given by one linear equation, or curved. The curved boundaries have not been computed to date; a classifier has been trained instead to distinguish the regions, so the partition has been known only approximately. In this paper we show that a curved boundary can be computed exactly, without solving any optimal control problem. The method rests on one property. Once the sequence of active constraints is fixed, together with the instants inside it at which a constraint becomes active or inactive (the switching times) and the instant at which the change of the neighboring region first appears (the event time), every condition on a boundary is a linear equation in the initial state, so the computation of a boundary, curved or not, is exact. We fix one of these instants, a switching time or the event time, and solve the linear equations that correspond to it for the corresponding initial state on the boundary; stepping the fixed instant along the horizon yields the whole boundary. A hyperplane is the case in which no instant is left to fix. We illustrate the method on the Newell-Lee evaporator, which has seven critical regions and eight boundaries, four hyperplanes and four curved, computing one boundary of each type in full with the adjacent regions at its ends.

title: Optimal Convergence of Quadratic Not-a-Knot Spline Interpolation on Arbitrary Partitions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32044v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The not-a-knot condition provides a simple spline interpolation scheme that requires no derivative data at the endpoints. Whereas the classical not-a-knot scheme using odd-degree splines selects knots that coincide with the data points, this approach does not extend to the even-degree case. In this paper we establish the well-posedness of the not-a-knot interpolation problem for even-degree splines, where knots are selected at midpoints of data values. We then show that the quadratic case, introduced in [M. J. D. Powell, Approximation Theory and Methods, Cambridge University Press, 1981], achieves $\mathcal{O}(h^3)$ convergence for $C^3$ functions on arbitrary partitions without mesh-ratio restrictions. The proof derives a linear system defining the interpolating spline, normalizes the system to bound the matrix norm of its inverse using a Neumann-series argument, and establishes global error bounds.

title: Piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation
authors: Rui Ma, Yang Xing, Shuo Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper develops a piecewise $P_2$ finite element space on rectangular meshes in arbitrary dimensions for the biharmonic equation. The discrete space imposes continuity of vertex sums on $(d-2)$-faces and of averaged normal derivatives across interior $(d-1)$-faces. A local algebraic characterization of $P_2$ is first established through the unisolvence of an enriched polynomial space and the resulting compatibility conditions. For each interior element, a $3^d$-element patch is then introduced, and the associated homogeneous patch space is shown to be one-dimensional. The corresponding patch functions, extended by zero, form a basis of the global homogeneous discrete space. A local quadratic interpolation operator is further constructed in arbitrary dimensions. Its approximation properties, together with a consistency estimate derived from the weak continuity conditions, lead to the optimal broken $H^2$ error estimate for the biharmonic problem.

title: A Dynamic Inventory Rationing Model for Last-Mile Delivery of Medication in Liberia's Community Health Program
authors: Baris Ata, Yufan Chen, Robert Montgomery
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the dynamic allocation of scarce medications in Liberia's community health program. A central warehouse supplies a health facility and the Community Health Assistants (CHAs) it supervises. When a CHA runs out of medication, patients are referred to the facility, incurring travel costs if they complete the referral and remain untreated otherwise. Allocating inventory to CHAs allows more patients to receive treatment without traveling, while retaining inventory centrally preserves flexibility to respond to uncertain demand. The allocation problem must balance these considerations while accounting for fairness across locations. We formulate this problem as a finite-horizon stochastic control problem whose objective combines the costs of referrals and untreated patients with a demand-weighted fairness utility. Because standard dynamic programming methods are computationally intractable in this setting, we develop a continuous-time approximation that involves controlling the drift rate of a reflected Brownian motion. We then adapt the deep splitting method, using deep neural networks to approximate the value function and its gradient and compute a dynamic allocation policy. We calibrate the model using data on malaria cases among children in the Fangonda region of Lofa County, Liberia, and evaluate the proposed policy in the original discrete-time model. In the baseline setting, our policy reduces operating costs by about 6% relative to the strongest benchmark, the fairness-only policy, while retaining approximately 98% of its fairness utility. Additional experiments show that higher referral costs shift inventory toward CHAs and reduce local unmet demand, while greater demand variability increases our policy's performance over the fairness-only benchmark. Our model and computational approach provide a framework for studying similar last-mile allocation problems.

title: Continuous-Time Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Control: Limits, Duality, and Stability
authors: Minjung Gim, Hee Jun Yang, Yeoneung Kim
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32080v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A sampled robust control problem averages future values over disturbance laws, while its continuous-time counterpart evolves with an averaged drift. We establish a fluid limit connecting these two models for Wasserstein ambiguity sets. Under a uniform disturbance moment bound and subcritical growth, sampled Bellman values converge locally uniformly to the upper and lower values of a discounted differential game. The argument accommodates unbounded disturbances without requiring square-integrable increments. We also derive an explicit bound on the change in either game value when both the radius and center of the ambiguity set vary. For Euclidean disturbance space, uniform Lipschitz continuity in the disturbance, common state and cost Lipschitz bounds, and a discount rate exceeding the drift's state Lipschitz constant, this estimate converts distributional confidence bounds into uniform value approximation bounds. Static Wasserstein duality reformulates pointwise distributional optimization; affine disturbance dependence permits an exact reduction to a ball of means. Experiments illustrate the common limit and decreasing value error with sample size. For a nonlinear disturbance model, uniform shifts overestimate worst-case recovery speed by about 36\%. In a two-product inventory model, increasing ambiguity raises production near balance while reducing the region of full production in deeper backlogs.

title: Timed Recovery Safe Gradient Flows for Constrained Nonlinear Programming
authors: Tianxi Luo, Yue Wu, Fei Chen, Hongsheng Qi
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper studies how to relax pointwise feasibility in continuous-time dynamics for inequality-constrained nonlinear programming while retaining a quantitative feasible-recovery guarantee. Existing safe gradient flows enforce forward invariance of the feasible set, which yields an anytime-feasible dynamics but can be overly restrictive for optimization because it suppresses transient infeasible motion that may be essential for effective descent. To address this limitation, we propose a timed recovery safe gradient flow that replaces pointwise feasibility with fixed-horizon feasible recovery. The proposed construction augments the state with a timer that records the elapsed infeasible duration and computes a minimum-norm correction to the nominal gradient flow through a pointwise convex quadratic program. We show that the resulting augmented safe set is forward invariant and that every trajectory initialized from the feasible set returns to it within every time window of length \(\tau\). We further show that, in a strict interior inactive regime, the closed-loop dynamics reduces exactly to the nominal gradient flow and recovers the corresponding local convergence behavior. Numerical examples illustrate how the recovery horizon shapes the closed-loop behavior and corroborate the theoretical analysis.

title: Covariance-Informed Ensemble Score Filtering: Embedding Localized Covariance Geometry into Score-Based Transport
authors: Siming Liang, Peter Jan van Leeuwen, Hristo G. Chipilski, Zezhong Zhang, Feng Bao, Guannan Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32148v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Background-error covariance models are central to atmospheric data assimilation because they spread partial observational information across space, variables, and dynamically coupled scales. Ensemble and variational methods exploit this covariance geometry efficiently, but their standard analysis formulations are largely built around Gaussian or locally quadratic approximations. Score-based ensemble filtering provides a framework for nonlinear distributional transport, but existing Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) formulations lack an intrinsic covariance-mediated pathway for propagating likelihood information from observed to unobserved state components. We introduce a covariance-informed ensemble score filter (CI-EnSF) that embeds localized forecast-error covariance geometry directly into the forward diffusion and reverse transport. The proposed forward diffusion is covariance-shaped in standardized state space and becomes isotropic under the corresponding control-variable transformation. This covariance structure continuously propagates observational information from observed to unobserved state components throughout the reverse transport analysis trajectory. Experiments with Lorenz-96 and surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) dynamics show a clear regime dependence. For linear observations, a well-tuned LETKF is more accurate, while CI-EnSF maintains stable cycling and effective covariance-mediated information propagation. Under strongly nonlinear observations and under climatological initialization, CI-EnSF achieves lower analysis error and greater cycling robustness than Gaussian ensemble benchmarks such as the LETKF, with improvements extending across spatial scales in the nonlinear SQG experiment. These results suggest that the principal benefit of CI-EnSF arises from combining nonlinear distributional transport with the mature covariance geometry used in conventional data assimilation.

title: A branch-and-filter method for mixed-integer linear programming
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a new tree-search framework for mixed-integer linear programming problems, which incorporates a filter mechanism as a node-acceptance device. The introduced branch-and-filter algorithm combines proper branching actions with a filter on integrality violation and an incumbent-dependent objective coordinate. Inspired by classical filter methods in nonconvex constrained optimization, the proposed method moves to a restoration phase whenever sufficient progress cannot be provided by the filter and funnel mechanisms, the latter of which is anchored at global relaxation lower bounds. Under mild assumptions, the introduced method either certifies infeasibility in finitely many iterations, or converges to global optimality. Moreover, we establish a total outer iteration complexity bound of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ to certification of an $\varepsilon$-optimal mixed-integer solution through fixed-integer linear programming recovery. We finally perform several numerical experiments to study the performance of branch-and-filter against benchmark solvers, under a branch-and-bound, a branch-and-cut, and a novel cell-deletion realization of the proposed restoration oracle.

title: Weak adversarial tensor neural network for high-dimensional Fokker-Planck equations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32169v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Solving high-dimensional stationary Fokker-Planck (SFP) equations remains challenging. Recently, deep learning methods have shown great potential for solving high-dimensional SFP equations due to their universal approximation and mesh-free training. However, the high-dimensional integrals involved in loss computation and normalization can be expensive to approximate accurately using Monte Carlo integration. To address this issue, we propose a weak adversarial tensor neural network (WATNN) method for solving high-dimensional SFP equations, which combines a weak adversarial (WA) formulation with the tensor neural network (TNN). The WA formulation avoids the cross terms introduced by squaring the strong residual, reducing the number of integrals to be computed. When both the primal network and the adversarial test network are set as TNNs, the TNN quadrature scheme provides accurate and efficient normalization and loss computation with relatively few fixed quadrature points, avoiding the statistical sampling error that arises when using Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the effectiveness numerically on four high-dimensional SFP equations. For the 6D unimodal, 6D multi-modal, 10D multi-modal and 20D multi-modal problems, WATNN achieves the mean relative errors of 1.50%, 1.13%, 1.20% and 7.93% respectively, in only a few minutes.

title: Block Toeplitz Operators, Matrix Valued Truncated Toeplitz operators, and Conjugations
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32170v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we characterize the complex symmetry of block Toeplitz operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H2(E) with conjugation C_{u,\lambda}, where E is a finite dimensional Hilbert space. We also extend the application of this conjugation to matrix valued truncated Toeplitz operators.

title: Encoding-Sensitive Nullstellensatz Certificates for Syndrome Exclusion in LDPC Codes: Sharp Local Bounds and a Linear Separation
authors: Malihe Aliasgari, Hassan Khodaiemehr, Khadijeh Bagheri
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32171v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Certifying that a parity-check matrix has no nonempty set of at most t variable nodes leaving at most b checks unsatisfied arises in minimum-distance and trapping-set analysis. Such absence is the infeasibility of a polynomial system, provable by an independently checkable Nullstellensatz certificate. The degree of these certificates depends strongly on how the two cardinality constraints are encoded, although the encodings have identical solutions. For a local encoding with inclusion-exclusion and cardinality obstructions, we construct explicit certificates of degree at most t + b + K + 1, with K logarithmic in the maximum check degree; this bound is independent of the block length and cannot be improved in general. For a standard counting encoding, a generalized planted-knapsack theorem, which pulls back a knapsack functional with an arbitrary target, gives lower bounds linear in the block length for cycle codes, regular codes of girth at least six near the feasibility boundary, array-based quasi-cyclic codes and minimum-distance certificates for arrays of circulant permutation matrices, where the local degree stays bounded. On array codes and regular codes of girth at least eight, planted column pairs extend these bounds to odd column weight with no unsatisfied checks. The planting argument is optimal among such pullbacks. All computed degrees and certificates are verified in exact rational arithmetic; bounds are distinguished from exact minimum degrees. Local certificates for quasi-cyclic matrices, including a lifted fifth-generation New Radio base graph, pass two independent verifiers.

title: Nadler Theorem on Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32240v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a generalized metric space endowed with a weighted graph and establish sufficient conditions for the existence of fixed points for set-valued mappings that satisfy a contractive condition only along the links of the graph. To demonstrate the applicability and significance of our results, several illustrative examples are presented. As an application, we establish the solvability of a class of integral problems involving set-valued data.

title: Distributed Attacker Assignment and Interception Control in Multi-Agent Target-Attacker-Defender Games
authors: Pengyang Fan, Shaoqing Zhang, Chao Zhai, Weiguo Xia
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32244v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper addresses the Target-Attacker-Defender (TAD) game within a planar environment, focusing on the protection of a stationary target against incoming threats. To compensate for potential speed disadvantages of the defenders, we leverage geometric pre-positioning within an annular defense perimeter. The problem is formulated as an area interception problem, for which we propose a distributed multi-agent algorithm consisting of two primary modules: target allocation and interception control. For target allocation, an equitable region partitioning strategy is employed to divide the defense area into annular sectors and assign defenders to attackers. Under specified angular-separation and parameter conditions, the proposed partitioning mechanism ensures that each defender is assigned at most one attacker, thereby reducing the complexity of multi-agent assignment. For the control layer, movement protocols based on zero-sum differential games and coverage optimization are designed, achieving Nash equilibrium strategies while maintaining effective barrier coverage. Numerical simulations show that the proposed method enables slower defenders to intercept faster attackers through proactive deployment and maintains nearly constant local computation time as the swarm size increases.

title: An energy-stable parametric finite element framework for surface diffusion with moving contact lines on curved substrates
authors: Harald Garcke, Robert N\"urnberg, Rong Tang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32270v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop energy-stable parametric finite element methods for surface diffusion of solid films with moving contact lines on curved substrates. Discretizing both the film surface and the substrate patches allows the introduction of linear schemes that are unconditionally energy stable. A nonlinear variant of the schemes ensures that, in addition, the vertices of the substrate approximations remain attached to the true substrate throughout. Moreover, our framework can incorporate anisotropic surface energy densities, for both the film surface and the substrate, as well as different tangential motions. Numerical experiments in two and three space dimensions illustrate the practicality of the introduced methods.

title: On the Algebraic Structure of Lewis Carroll's Logic -- Behind the Looking Glass: A Mathematical Perspective
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32273v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Charles Ludwidge Dodgeson, better known by his literary pen name `Lewis Carroll', has a number of well known and cherished literary works to his credit, for example "Alice in Wonderland" and "Through the Looking Glass". Apart from this he is known to have a strong professional interest in mathematics and logic with an inclination towards an educational and recreational perspective.
  In this work we consider the algebraic structure behind Lewis Carroll's approach to classical logic and his logical puzzles. Starting with the arithmetic of $0$ and $1$, we develop the connections between Boolean-valued functions, sets and predicates, which we refer to as the "entangled trinity". This provides a common setting in which Carroll's approach and Boole's perspective can be understood. Particular attention is given to what is meant by "the conclusion" of a logical problem. We suggest a precise interpretation of a complete conclusion in terms of largest lower bounds involving only the predicates to be retained, thereby sharpening Carroll's approach. The role of natural language in choosing a suitable universe and identifying these predicates is discussed through a variety of examples. Finally, we present computerised solution methods, including the use of Boolean satisfiability solvers for larger puzzles.

title: Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection Reinforcement Learning Problems for a Markov Regime-Switching System with No-Shorting Constraints
authors: Minghui Zhang, Xun Li, Xin Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32301v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper is the first to study the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio selection problem with no-shorting constraints in a Markov regime-switching market using reinforcement learning (RL). The main challenge stems from the interaction between random regime shifts and portfolio non-negativity constraints, which typically causes the coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equations to lose smoothness across different state regions. Additionally, directly imposing no-shorting constraints on randomized policies disrupts their analytically tractable Gaussian structure, complicating both exploratory modeling and reinforcement learning. To address these challenges, we propose an auxiliary exploratory approach that limits the policy to a Gaussian distribution and applies the no-shorting constraint solely to its mean. We explicitly characterize the optimal policy for this auxiliary problem and demonstrate that, by appropriately selecting the exploration variance, its optimal mean policy exactly matches the optimal policy of the original constrained mean-variance problem. Building upon this analytical framework, we develop a model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the optimal portfolio policy directly from trajectory data. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and show that the proposed method can effectively recover the optimal no-shorting portfolio in a regime-switching market.

title: A stochastic mirror descent algorithm for mean-field control problems
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32303v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We develop a stochastic mirror descent method for continuous-time McKean-Vlasov control with measure-valued controls and general Bregman regularisation. The dependence on the state law leads to a coupled Wasserstein-Bregman stability problem and to a McKean-Vlasov adjoint equation, which have no counterpart in classical stochastic control. We establish a first-order representation of the cost and prove its relative smoothness in two regimes: nonlinear dynamics with bounded cost derivatives, and affine state-law dynamics with linearly growing cost derivatives, the latter covering linear-quadratic (LQ) and more general nonquadratic models. Our regularity conditions in the control measure are formulated through directional finite increments and do not require second-order flat derivatives. We further introduce relative semiconvexity along admissible forward-backward trajectories, allowing compensation between the dynamics, running cost, and terminal cost beyond pointwise Hamiltonian convexity. This yields energy dissipation, an O(1/n) convergence rate at the convexity threshold, and geometric convergence when regularisation dominates relative nonconvexity. Explicit LQ criteria and numerical experiments illustrate the scope of the results.

title: A domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase CO$_2$ sequestration with moving wells
authors: Xin He, Xianda Shen, Lei Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32340v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present a domain-decomposition reduced-order model for two-phase geological CO$_2$ storage with fixed and moving wells. The approach builds on a nonoverlapping Schur formulation of a conservative RT0--P0 discretization solved by a sequential pressure--transport algorithm. The distinctive feature of the formulation is that local reduced models are coupled through physically meaningful interface variables: pressure traces for the pressure solve and inflow saturation traces for the transport solve. To address moving wells, we introduce a well-aware strategy that combines source-response enrichment, HAPOD-based far-field compression, and hybrid full-order/reduced-order treatment of well and near-well subdomains. We also formulate conservation-oriented hyper-reduction rules where interface fluxes, boundary terms and source terms are protected. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate accuracy, computational efficiency, robustness of the overall methodology.

title: Long-time stability and convergence of a BDF3 method for a parabolic equation with fading memory
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32364v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We analyze the long-time stability and convergence of a third-order backward differentiation formula (BDF3) for parabolic equations with exponentially fading memory. The BDF3 scalar resolvent has oscillatory coefficients, so the monotonicity argument used for lower-order formulas in [Math. Comp. 62 (1994) 477-496] does not apply. We instead control memory feedback by the absolute mass of its discrete Green sequence and establish the rigorous stability-constant bounds $23/20<\Lambda_3<579/500$. A causal third-order memory quadrature with nonnegative assembled weights then yields exponentially weighted stability without a parabolic step-size restriction. With third-order starting values, we prove a uniform-in-time third-order temporal error estimate and extend it to conforming finite elements. Numerical tests confirm the predicted convergence orders and the long-time behavior.

title: Global injectivity and real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$
authors: Xinhao Hu, Jaume Llibre, Yilei Tang
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32391v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we study the global injectivity of local diffeomorphisms in $\mathbb{R}^n$, extending the criterions of Braun and Llibre in [{\it Pacific J. Math.} {\bf 333} (2024) 1--15] from the planar radial case to arbitrary dimension. Then we extend the results of Llibre and Mello in [{\it Bull. Sci. Math.} {\bf 213} (2026) 103889] to arbitrary dimension, obtaining two necessary and sufficient conditions for the real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$ by qualitative theory of differential equations. Finally, using weighted Poincar\'e compactification in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we provide a sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture.

title: MIACE and Monotone Tracking: Exact Tuning for First-Order Plants and Positive Cascades with Pure Delay
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32401v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Module of Integral Absolute Complex Error (MIACE) was created by me 23 years ago. It gave very nice behaviour to the transient response of the controlled systems I tested. It combines absolute tracking-error and equilibrium-centered command areas. For a stable unit-gain plant with known pure delay, an exact identity separates squared MIACE excess into a negative-area penalty and a weighted area imbalance. The resulting lower bound depends on the plant's first low-frequency moment and the delay. Every attaining response of a positive cascade is monotone, independently of controller structure. For a first-order plant, output variation and peak overshoot also admit quantitative bounds. Exact conditions identify the unique positive PI controller attaining the delayed bound; filtered PID extends attainment beyond this PI range. For cascades of arbitrary order, Hermite interpolation and a finite-support delay remainder construct proper rational controllers of the same order, with internal exponential stability proved by positive convolution representations. An exponential-moment characterization then closes the attainment question when internal delay blocks are allowed: an ordinary command attains the bound if and only if $\alpha>\mu+\delta-1$. An explicit internal-model controller realizes every feasible weight and delay. A sharp amplitude-cap condition determines the least command peak among all attaining responses and the complete capped sign-preserving area front. A small-gain estimate supplies an explicit MIACE deviation bound under delay error. A storage balance also extends the exact MIACE identity and monotone attainment to a nonlinear first-order class without delay. Independent physical integrations retain delays exactly; quadratic comparisons provide complementary benchmarks.

title: On the Limits of Stochastic Push-Pull over Time-Varying Digraphs
authors: Feiming Wang, Yutong He, Sulaiman Alghunaim, Kun Yuan
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32422v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Stochastic Push-Pull achieves linear speedup with respect to the network size $n$ on static strongly connected digraphs, but whether this speedup persists on time-varying networks remains unclear. In this work, we construct a quadratic decentralized problem on period-two networks showing that stochastic Push-Pull may fail to attain linear speedup over time-varying digraphs. For $p$-periodic networks, we identify an effective node count $n_{\mathrm{eff}}\le n$ that governs the leading stochastic term. Specifically, for smooth nonconvex objectives, we establish convergence upper bounds and matching lower bounds for stochastic Push-Pull with constant stepsizes, both exhibiting the leading-order dependence $\Theta(1/\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{eff}} T})$. When $p=1$, the identity $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=n$ recovers the usual linear speedup for static digraphs. However, periodic networks can have $n_{\mathrm{eff}}=o(n)$, demonstrating the loss of linear speedup under temporal variation. Numerical experiments illustrate effective-count scaling and the separation between static and periodic networks, consistent with our theoretical findings.

title: On the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set: monotone and measure preserving maps
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32424v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Let $E$ be the Cantor set, $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(E)$, let $P\le G$ be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and $L\le G$ the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. We study how $G$ is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that $G=LP=PL$. We show that this is not the case, in fact $PL$ and $LP$ are two different proper subsets of $G$. On the other hand, $PL$ is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of $G$, the multiplication map $P\times L\to PL$ is a homeomorphism, and $G=PLP=LPL$. In particular, every homeomorphism of $E$ is conjugate to an element of $PL$. We classify the double cosets $PgL$ using special clopen values set. There are continuum many of them, and $PL$ is the only one which is not meager. We prove that $G$ is topologically generated by one element of $P$ and one element of $L$ and these two generators produce the Thompson's group $V$. We also show that the generic homeomorphism of $E$ is the product of a generic element of $P$ and a generic element of $L$. The equality $G=PL$ fails also if $\lambda$ is replaced by any other full nonatomic measure.

title: $L$-tauberian operators and subspaces with equi-integrable unit ball
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the class $LW_+$ of $L$-tauberian operators and its dual counterpart, the class $MW_-$ of $M$-cotauberian operators. We obtain sequential, perturbative, and algebraic characterizations of these classes. As a consequence, every $T\in LW_+(E,Y)$ is disjointly non-singular, and the converse implication holds if and only if every dispersed subspace of $E$ has equi-integrable unit ball. For $E=L_p$, the latter property depends on $p$. For $1\leq p<2$, equi-integrability of the unit ball is equivalent to dispersedness, and $L$-tauberian operators coincide with disjointly non-singular operators, while for $p\geq 2$ these equivalences fail. Moreover, $LW_+(L_p)$ is neither open nor stable under composition. Applying a result of Haydon, Odell, and Schlumprecht, we show that for $2

<\infty$ every infinite dimensional dispersed subspace of $L_p$ contains an infinite dimensional subspace with equi-integrable unit ball. However, we give an example showing that this is not true for $p=2$.

title: Partial rigidity and q-additive functions
abstract:
arXiv:2610.32445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A system $(X,\mu, T)$ is partially rigid with constant $\delta>0$ if there exists an incresing sequence $(n_k)$ such that $\displaystyle \liminf_{k \to \infty } \mu(A \cap T^{-n_k}A) \geq \delta \mu(A)$ for every measurable $A \subset X$. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from $q$-additive functions $\pmod M$ in terms of quantities arising from B\'esineau's theorem. With this, we build a family of strongly $q$-additive functions to deduce that the collection of partial rigidity rates for substitution subshifts is dense in $[0,1]$ answering a question of Donoso, Maass and the author.
